paras: The killing of James Biddle was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Deputy Sheriff Bunnell at Bunnell Station, in southern St. Johns County, Florida, on or about August 22, 1900. According to a St. Augustine wire report, the only account found, Biddle had attempted to kill a woman and fired on the deputy before being shot through the heart as he ran. The item circulated in white papers in Georgia, South Carolina and Mississippi and in the Black Richmond Planet.

Word of the shooting reached St. Augustine from Bunnell Station, a settlement in the southern part of the county. The wire item described Biddle as "a desperate negro and gambler" and said he "attempted to kill a woman" when the deputy interfered. In this version Biddle "fired upon him and ran," and Bunnell "dropped Biddle with a shot through the heart," killing him instantly. The woman is not named, and no account from her, from witnesses or from Biddle's side appears in the coverage.
No report of an inquest, an investigation of the deputy, or any further proceedings was found.

The Savannah Morning News carried the story first, on August 24, under the headline "Bunnell Killed Biddle" and the subhead "Deputy Sheriff Fired Upon a Desperate Florida Negro." The Sumter Watchman and Southron reprinted the full text on August 29 with an August 23 dateline. Two Mississippi weeklies ran a shortened version headed "Desperate Negro Killed," which dropped the claim that Biddle had fired on the officer and said only that the officer interfered. All of the white papers presented the deputy's account as fact.

The Richmond Planet, a Black weekly, printed the full wire text word for word on September 1, dated August 24, among short items in its "General Southern News" column. It kept the phrase "desperate negro" and added no comment, so the Black-press version did not differ from the white wire report.

Copies of the wire disagree on its dateline, August 23 in the Sumter paper and August 24 in the Richmond Planet, so the killing took place on August 22 or 23. Because the Savannah paper had the story in its August 24 issue, the August 23 dateline is the more likely original.

reader.title: Killing of James Biddle
bases: A deputy sheriff acting alone shot and killed Biddle after, by the wire account, intervening when Biddle attempted to kill a woman; no mob or crowd is mentioned (A1, A5).

All five reports are copies or abridgements of one St. Augustine wire item based on news that 'reached here', and no independent local, inquest or Black-correspondent account was found (A1, A2, A3, A4, A5).

accounts.label: St. Augustine wire report (officer's side)
accounts.gist: Biddle attempted to kill a woman; the deputy interfered, Biddle fired on him and ran, and Bunnell shot him through the heart.

accounts.label: Abridged wire report
accounts.gist: Biddle attempted to kill a woman and the officer interfered; Biddle was shot and killed, with no mention that he fired first or ran.

framing.detail: Headlines 'Bunnell Killed Biddle' and 'Desperate Negro Killed' accepted the deputy's account and labeled Biddle 'a desperate negro and gambler'.
The Richmond Planet ran the wire text word for word, including 'desperate negro', in a news-brief column with no comment.
